title: Integer multiplication on abelian Picard classes modulo algebraic equivalence
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] and $A/k$ an abelian variety [def-sc-abelian-variety]. Let $N$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_A$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. For every integer $n\geq0$, let $[n]_A:A\to A$ be the sum of $n$ copies of the identity under the group law, with $[0]_A$ the constant identity morphism. Then
$$[n]_A^*N\otimes(N^\vee)^{\otimes n^2}$$
is algebraically equivalent to $\mathcal O_A$. Here $N^\vee=\mathcal Hom(N,\mathcal O_A)$ is the dual line, tensor powers with exponent zero mean $\mathcal O_A$, pullback is tensor inverse image [def-pc-module-pullback], and tensor is the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Algebraic equivalence is the equivalence relation on invertible-module isomorphism classes generated by pairs of fibres of an invertible module on $A\times_k T$, where $T$ is a smooth connected $k$-variety. No symmetry, ampleness or restriction on the characteristic or on $n$ is imposed.

source.place: Chapter I §10, Remark 10.19, printed p.50; multiplication acts as n squared on NS(A)=Pic(A)/Pic^0(A), using Corollary 5.4. The displayed line-module formulation is the equality of these classes.

proof.text: Tensoring a family on $A\times T$ by the pullback of a fixed line gives a family connecting the tensor products of its two fibres. Dualizing a family connects their duals. Thus algebraic equivalence is a congruence for the tensor group of line classes. Write $G$ for the quotient group, $c_j$ for the class of $[j]^*N$ ($j\geq0$), and $c_{-1}$ for the class of $[-1]^*N$. An identity-fibre basis trivializes $[0]^*N$, so $c_0=0$ and $c_1=[N]$. Tensor pullback and composition in [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor] justify these fibre identifications.

source.place: I Remark 10.19; line-class interpretation of NS(A)

proof.text: Put $D=[-1]^*N\otimes N^\vee$. The statement of [lem-sfb-abelian-polarization-calculus] gives $\phi_{[-1]^*N}=\phi_N$ and $\phi_L(a)=[t_a^*L\otimes L^{-1}]$. Hence for each $a\in A(k)$ the two translated-difference lines for $[-1]^*N$ and $N$ are isomorphic. Taking their tensor quotient and distributing pullback by [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor] gives $t_a^*D\otimes D^\vee\cong\mathcal O_A$, that is $t_a^*D\cong D$. This is translation invariance of the actual line $D$, not merely equality modulo algebraic equivalence.

source.place: I Remark 10.19, inversion acts as the identity; I §§8–9 for the defining homomorphism

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-abelian-homogeneous-line-algebraic-triviality] to $D$. Its hypotheses hold over the given algebraically closed field and for every translation by step 2. Therefore $D$ is algebraically trivial and $c_{-1}=c_1$ in $G$.

source.place: I §8 Proposition 8.4, Remark 8.7(c), Proposition 8.14; I Remark 10.19

proof.text: For each $r\geq1$, pull [thm-sc-theorem-of-cube] back along $A\to A^3$, $x\mapsto([r]x,x,-x)$. The three single maps are $[r],1,[-1]$, the double sums are $[r+1],[r-1],[0]$, and the triple sum is $[r]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor], its identity becomes $([r]^*N)^{\otimes2}\otimes N\otimes[-1]^*N\cong[r+1]^*N\otimes[r-1]^*N\otimes[0]^*N$. Passing to $G$ and using steps 1 and 3 yields $c_{r+1}=2c_r-c_{r-1}+2c_1$.

source.place: I Corollary 5.4 proof, equation (2), printed pp.22–23; cube identity is also Stacks Tag 0BFE (groupoids.tex, lemma-apply-cube)

proof.text: Induct on consecutive indices, starting with $c_0=0$ and $c_1=c_1$. If $c_{r-1}=(r-1)^2c_1$ and $c_r=r^2c_1$, the recurrence gives $c_{r+1}=(2r^2-(r-1)^2+2)c_1=(r+1)^2c_1$. Consequently $c_n=n^2[N]$ for every $n\geq0$, so the displayed tensor quotient in the statement is algebraically trivial. This uses integer arithmetic in $G$ and divides by no integer, including in positive characteristic.

proof_origin.place: I Remark 10.19, with the recurrence of Corollary 5.4, pp.22–23, and the homogeneous Pic^0 criterion in §8, pp.35–40

The item is unchanged and true. Checked against Milne AV I Remark 10.19 (p.50) and Corollary 5.4 with its recurrence (2) (pp.22-23). Steps: (1) algebraic equivalence is a ⊗/dual congruence, and [0]=e∘π so c_0=0; elementary. (2) polarization-calculus states φ_{[-1]^*L}=φ_L and φ_L(x)=[t_x^*L⊗L^{-1}], so t_a^*D≅D for D=[-1]^*N⊗N^∨. (3) The new node gives c_{-1}=c_1. (4) Pulling the cube theorem back along ([r],1,[-1]) gives sums [r],[r+1],[r-1],[0], and I checked c_{r+1}=2c_r-c_{r-1}+2c_1 myself, sign included. (5) Two-base induction with 2r^2-(r-1)^2+2=(r+1)^2 and no division, so characteristic p is fine. New node lem-sfb-abelian-homogeneous-line-algebraic-triviality: homogeneous implies algebraically trivial, true by Milne 8.4(b) and the Pic^0 definition, Remark 8.7(c) A^∨(k)=Pic^0 with the Poincaré family over a connected smooth A^∨, or 8.14 with Λ(M). Tested on Spec k and on degree-0 and positive-degree lines on an elliptic curve. It is not a duplicate: polarization-calculus, space-poincare-calculus, projective-picard-identity-representability, algebraically-trivial-line-multiplicativity and picard-square-triviality prove only the converse or representability, and lem-sc-mult-n-pullback covers only symmetric N. It is statement-only and self-contained, with searches recorded. Accepted tool_use: lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor (Lean-closed). Batch-5: the lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry route (generic Proj Sym quotient functor, 01OB) and the def-trf-schematically-dense-open route (plain definition) are generic and outside the trace-formula and Poincaré-duality assumptions.
